cards.title: Keep shipment paperwork and the carrier receipt for FBA pallets
cards.summary: Retain the bill of lading and the driver's pickup receipt for every FBA pallet so you can prove shipment if Amazon reports inventory missing.
cards.use_when: Fulfillment: preparing or dispatching an FBA pallet shipment and setting up your record-keeping for inbound inventory.
steps: Print the BOL (bill of lading) from the individual shipment summary in Seller Central; the driver needs it at pickup to verify they are taking the correct pallet. Missing required paperwork can trigger a fee.
File every receipt and paper connected to the shipment, however unimportant it seems, in one consistent place.
When the driver collects the pallet, get the pickup receipt and store it with the BOL. This is your proof the full pallet left your premises.

If Amazon later claims it never received the shipment, retrieve the receipt to open a reconciliation case. The source recounts a pallet that was reported missing for months and would have cost over $10,000; it was eventually found and re-added, but only after a long delay.
Verify current BOL and reconciliation requirements inside Seller Central before each shipment, since Amazon's inbound workflow changes.
caveats: The $10,000 figure is the presenter's own loss experience, not a typical loss rate.
Without the carrier receipt, a lost-shipment claim is much harder to win.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Call the carrier and pickup location the day before an FBA pallet pickup
cards.summary: Confirm truck type, liftgate or forklift needs, dock access and arrival window the day before pickup to avoid failed collections.
cards.use_when: Fulfillment: scheduling a pallet pickup from a home, warehouse or manufacturer for FBA inbound.
steps: Read the BOL to identify which trucking company is collecting the pallet, then phone them the day before pickup.
If pickup is at a residential address, tell them so they dispatch a smaller truck; an oversized truck at a house causes problems.
If you have no forklift at the pickup site, request a truck with a liftgate so the pallet can be lowered and loaded.
If pickup is at a warehouse or manufacturer, call ahead and ask whether they have a loading dock or forklift, and request a liftgate truck if not.
Confirm the arrival time and make sure someone can be present: you at home, or a manufacturer employee if the goods ship from the factory.
Re-verify the carrier's current booking and appointment process, as interface and requirements may change.
caveats: Applies to pallet/LTL freight rather than small-parcel FBA shipments.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Send roughly three to six months of FBA inventory and reorder at two to three months
cards.summary: Keep FBA stock between about three and six months of cover so you avoid both monthly storage and long-term storage fees and out-of-stock rank damage.
cards.use_when: Replenishment: deciding how many units to ship into FBA on each inbound and when to trigger the next production order.
steps: Estimate your monthly unit sales, then ship approximately three to six months of cover in each inbound shipment rather than a full year.
Avoid over-shipping: excess units sit in the warehouse and incur monthly storage fees, and the source states long-term storage fees kick in beyond six months of aged inventory.

Avoid under-shipping in competitive categories: running out of stock can lower your product's ranking or, in the presenter's experience, leave sellers unable to recover, and Amazon may blacklist the account.
Start the next replenishment order when remaining stock approaches the two-to-three-month mark so new units arrive before stockout while aged inventory stays under the long-term fee threshold.
Confirm current Amazon storage-fee tiers and long-term aged-inventory thresholds in Seller Central before committing, since fee structures change.
caveats: Three-to-six months is the presenter's recommendation, not a published Amazon rule.
Seasonal demand, lead time and cash flow may justify different cover; treat this as a heuristic to adjust.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Optimize the search-result click drivers: main image, title keywords, price and review count
cards.summary: Amazon ranks on click-through and conversion, so tune the only elements shoppers see in search results and put your target keywords into the title.
cards.use_when: Product listing/SEO: creating or refreshing an Amazon listing title and main image before and during launch.
steps: Recognize that in Amazon search results a shopper sees only your main image, title, price and number of reviews; these drive the click.

Write the title to contain the exact keyword phrase you want to rank for, so Amazon reads the listing as relevant to that query (the source example uses 'cocktail flashcards' where both words appear in the title).
Optimize the main image for the same target shopper's query, since a stronger image raises click-through.
Support conversion after the click with review volume and rating, because Amazon infers a review-rich product is more likely to satisfy buyers.
Treat click-through and conversion as the mechanism: products Amazon expects to be purchased rank higher, so improve both rather than chasing a single ranking trick.
caveats: The source treats keyword-in-title as a ranking input; Amazon's exact ranking weights are not disclosed and change over time.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Build launch-day sales velocity because Amazon rewards early sales spikes
cards.summary: Concentrate sales into launch day and the first weeks to signal demand and trigger a ranking snowball, since the top search positions take most sales.
cards.use_when: Acquisition: planning a new Amazon product launch and setting launch-day sales targets.
steps: Aim to generate as many sales as possible on day one rather than spreading them thinly, because a sudden sales-velocity spike signals to Amazon that the product is in demand.
Stack multiple traffic sources into the launch window (social audience, email list, giveaway buyers, influencers, early PPC) so the velocity signal is concentrated.
Expect a feedback loop: higher rank brings more impressions, more sales and further rank gains, which the presenter describes as a snowball and as the core of the launch.
Accept that lower search positions receive progressively fewer sales, so the launch objective is ranking, not just the first day's revenue.
Note the presenter's own example launched one product with over $11,000 in sales on day one; treat this as an anecdote, not a benchmark.
caveats: The presenter's $11,000 day-one figure is a personal case, not an expected outcome.
Velocity tactics must still comply with Amazon's terms; incentivized-review methods carry account risk.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Warm an audience before launch with social content plus an email waitlist
cards.summary: Post niche content on TikTok/Instagram/Facebook/YouTube, funnel viewers to an email waitlist, and email the list on launch day.
cards.use_when: Acquisition: building pre-launch demand and a launch-day traffic source for a new Amazon product.
steps: Pick the platforms you will actually maintain; the presenter rates TikTok as the easiest for reach and suggests repurposing the same short videos to Instagram Reels and Facebook, or choosing YouTube or a podcast if preferred.
Put a link in each bio or video description directing viewers to join a waitlist rather than straight to the not-yet-live Amazon listing.
Start engaging the list one to three months before launch, emailing updates and building anticipation like a film marketing campaign.
Offer a sweepstakes entry for a free unit to give people a concrete reason to join the list, using a tool such as Rebate to host the giveaway entry form.
On launch day, email the list with a direct link to the Amazon listing so purchase takes one click.
The source cites a student using TikTok for a cocktail-cards product reaching over $140,000 in sales in the first three months; treat as an example only.
caveats: The $140,000 result is a single case, not a forecast.
Sweepstakes rules vary by platform and jurisdiction; confirm compliance.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Run a pre-launch Facebook group to get product feedback and build commitment
cards.summary: A Facebook group beats a pure email list because members interact, give product feedback, and feel committed to buying at launch.
cards.use_when: Acquisition/merchandising: gathering buyer input on a product before finalizing it and creating a launch-day audience.
steps: Create a Facebook group for people interested in the product category before launch, instead of relying only on an email list.
Post questions in the group such as what members think of the current product or packaging, and harvest the comments to improve the product and listing.
Let members interact with each other so they see other excited buyers, which the presenter treats as stronger than a one-way email list.
Advantage of groups over pages: posts in groups are more likely to be shown to members than page posts.
When the product goes live, post in the group that it is available and link to the Amazon listing.
Use consistency: members who have participated and engaged are more likely to follow through and purchase at launch.
caveats: The source frames the group as producing a community effect; no measured conversion figures are given.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Recruit small influencers with free product and use a podcast to build relationships
cards.summary: Find 5,000–10,000-follower creators in your niche, offer free product for a post, and interview influencers on your podcast so they reciprocate with promotion.
cards.use_when: Acquisition/creative strategy: sourcing creator content and launch-day traffic for an Amazon product without a paid ad budget.
steps: Search Instagram, YouTube and TikTok for your niche and message creators directly asking whether they would post a photo or video in exchange for a free product.
Target the roughly 5,000–10,000 follower range for unpaid collaborations: the source says these creators are new enough not to charge and have a small, dedicated audience.
Budget to pay larger-audience creators when their reach justifies it; the source says this can be worthwhile, not that free always wins.
Use 'spotlight marketing': start a podcast and invite these creators as guests, building a relationship that makes them more likely to promote your product for free.
Ship product to confirmed creators ahead of launch so posts land in the launch window.
The presenter sent 85 boxes to influencers for one launch and credits it with a strong launch-day effect; treat as one case.
caveats: Niche and performance vary; the 5,000–10,000 range is the presenter's free-work sweet spot, not a rule.
Verify each platform's current disclosure and gifting rules before running creator campaigns.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Use Amazon Live and one-click shoppable video to convert viewers directly
cards.summary: Amazon Live puts an influencer talking about your product next to a buy link, so viewers purchase in one click while watching.
cards.use_when: Acquisition/creative strategy: adding a live or video shopping channel to a launch plan or ongoing traffic mix.
steps: Identify creators who host Amazon Live streams and are relevant to your category, using influencer discovery tools such as Rebate to shortlist them.
Offer free product and, where appropriate, payment for a mention so the host features your listing in a live stream.
Prefer Amazon Live over off-Amazon live platforms when purchase friction matters: viewers watch on Amazon and can buy with one click from the stream.
Cross-apply the same creators to YouTube, Instagram and other platforms where they will talk about the product if a live slot is not available.
Treat live shopping as an early-stage, less-crowded channel in the source's framing, so test it with a small number of creators before scaling.
caveats: The source calls this untapped; that is a point-in-time opinion and availability, requirements and fees can change.
Gift-and-review or paid-mention arrangements must follow Amazon's and the platform's disclosure rules.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Prefer organic growth to incentivized purchase-review schemes
cards.summary: The source describes giving refunds for keyword searches and reviews as gray-hat and technically against Amazon's terms, so weigh account risk before copying it.
cards.use_when: Launch/retention strategy: deciding whether to pursue review velocity through incentivized purchases and outdoor recruiting.
steps: The described tactic: approach people in bars, gyms or coffee shops, offer to reimburse their purchase via PayPal or Venmo, and ask them to leave a five-star review.
Have the recruited buyer search your target keyword on Amazon first, find your product, buy it and review it, so the sales attach to the keyword you want to rank for.
Collect contact details and follow up over the following one to three weeks to confirm the review was actually left.

A second described tactic is asking friends and family to buy and review; the source says this is usually fine but warns you must never have shared an internet connection between your seller account and their buyer account, or risk a ban.

Decide from a position of risk awareness: the source states this is technically against Amazon's terms of service and could lead to account shutdown, though they say it almost never happens for this kind of activity.
caveats: Incentivized reviews violate Amazon's terms and can result in enforcement; the presenter is describing a gray-hat practice, not recommending it.
Shared Wi-Fi or networks between seller and reviewer accounts is a specific, documented risk factor.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Start with an automatic Amazon PPC campaign, then move to manual targeting
cards.summary: Automatic campaigns let Amazon pick relevant keywords while you learn what converts, then manual keyword campaigns become more profitable.
cards.use_when: Acquisition/paid search: launching Amazon advertising for a new or newly launched product.
steps: In Seller Central open the advertising menu and campaign manager, choose Sponsored Products and create a campaign and ad group.
Name the ad group by intent (the source names one 'close match'), select the product to advertise, and let Amazon auto-target keywords relevant to your listing.
Run the automatic campaign first when you do not yet know which search phrases drive purchases; use its search-term data to discover converting queries.
Use the data to build manual keyword-targeted campaigns for the phrases that actually produced sales, which the source says is more profitable long term.
Add product targeting campaigns so your ads appear on competitor listings, and add negative keywords to stop paying for irrelevant clicks.
Note the source's claim that well-run Amazon PPC can return four to five dollars per dollar spent; that is a presenter aspiration, not a guarantee.
Verify the current campaign manager interface before setting up, as ad console layouts change.
caveats: Pay-per-click means you pay on every click whether or not it converts, so irrelevant targeting burns budget.
The 4–5x ROAS figure is presented as an upside example, not a benchmark.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Use negative keywords and relevance to avoid paying for junk clicks
cards.summary: Negative keywords block searches where your ad would spend money without selling, and only relevant search phrases should receive your bids.
cards.use_when: Acquisition/paid search: managing an Amazon PPC campaign's spend and search-term report after launch.
steps: Only let your product appear on searches relevant to what you sell; the source notes people click random results, so irrelevant impressions drain budget without sales.
Set up negative keywords to explicitly tell Amazon which searches your ad must not appear on; the presenter calls this one of the most important and most neglected PPC steps.
Build the negative list from the automatic campaign's search-term data, excluding queries that generated clicks but no orders.
Pair this with product-targeting campaigns on competitor detail pages, where the audience is already shopping the category.
Review the search-term report regularly and move spend from junk queries to converting ones rather than letting auto-targeting run unchecked.
caveats: Blocking too aggressively can suppress discovery in the early learning phase; review before adding negatives.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Enroll in Brand Registry for A+ content, video and conversion lift
cards.summary: Brand Registry unlocks A+ content pages, product videos and other modules that raise listing conversion, which in turn supports ranking.
cards.use_when: Product page/merchandising: building or upgrading an Amazon detail page and deciding which Brand-Registry-only modules to use.
steps: Enroll in Brand Registry before selling seriously, then open A+ Content Manager and replace the plain text description with image and infographic modules.
Add video to the listing: A+ content and video modules let shoppers see the product in use, which the source says increases purchase likelihood.
Why it matters for ranking: the source argues higher conversion per click leads Amazon to place the listing higher in search.
Use subscribe and save for consumable or repeat-use products, offering a discount for recurring deliveries on a schedule the customer chooses (monthly, bi-monthly, quarterly).
Use customer engagement tools to send targeted email campaigns to past buyers to raise retention.
Confirm current module availability and eligibility in Seller Central, as Brand Registry features change.
caveats: The claim that A+ content improves ranking follows from conversion, not from a published Amazon ranking factor.
Subscribe and save suits replenishable products; the source names food and drink as the clear fits.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Apply for Brand Registry with a trademark and a product listing in place
cards.summary: You need a pending or registered trademark, ownership verification and an active seller account, plus an existing ASIN and a branded product image.
cards.use_when: Brand setup: preparing a Brand Registry application before or shortly after launching an Amazon product.
steps: Get a trademark first: a text-based (word) mark or an image-based (logo) mark; the source says logo marks are generally easier to obtain when the product name is generic or crowded (e.g. 'performance nut butter' versus a distinctive logo).

File yourself at uspto.gov for around $275 by choosing your product category, uploading the image and entering the text on it; or hire a lawyer for typically a few hundred to a couple thousand dollars more.
Before applying, create the product listing so you have an ASIN: the application asks for your top-selling ASINs per category, and the source says the listing does not need to be perfect.

Go to the Brand Registry signup flow, sign in, choose 'enroll a new brand', enter the brand name exactly as it appears on the trademark, select the trademark office and enter the registration or serial number.

Upload a photo clearly showing the brand on the actual product packaging. The source's shortcut: print stickers of your branding onto competitor packaging with similar dimensions to create a convincing mockup when the product is not yet produced.
Verify ownership via the emailed code, answer the distribution questions (do you sell to distributors, where are products distributed, do you license your trademark), and submit.
Approval can take a couple of weeks and you may need to reapply; enrollment requirements and the interface should be verified at brandservices.amazon.com before starting.
caveats: The sticker-on-competitor-packaging mockup is a workaround the presenter used; the image must still convincingly show your branding on packaging.
You cannot complete the application without an existing listing/ASIN.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Use Brand Registry protections and programs to stop hijackers and cut fees
cards.summary: Brand Registry enables violation reporting, Transparency codes, brand referral bonus and escalated IP cases that protect listings from counterfeiters and hijackers.
cards.use_when: Retention/risk management: ongoing account and listing protection once a branded product is selling on Amazon.
steps: Report violations when someone copies your product or infringes your IP; Brand Registry establishes you as the rights owner so Amazon can act and remove counterfeit listings.
Enroll in the brand referral bonus, which the source says cuts the referral fee from 15% to 5% on qualifying branded sales (a $100 sale drops from $15 to $5 in fees in their example).
Sign up for the Vine program to obtain up to 30 trusted, detailed reviews; the source says it is free for brand-registered sellers versus the usual fee.
Use Transparency codes (the source cites up to 2,000 free codes) so authentic units carry a code; units without it can be flagged, which helps block counterfeit sellers of your ASIN.

Use sponsored brands (banner ads at the top of search), which the source says needs about three SKUs to use properly, and set up an Amazon storefront as a custom branded landing page reachable from your brand name.
Rely on Brand Registry as your escalation path if a hijacker edits your listing: you can prove ownership and get cases resolved faster.
Confirm current program fees, bonus percentages and code allowances in Seller Central; these figures referenced by the source can change.
caveats: The 15%-to-5% referral-fee reduction, free Vine, and 2,000 transparency codes are the source's stated figures and should be treated as time-sensitive.
Brand Registry reduces but does not eliminate the risk of hijacking or counterfeiting.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Read Brand Analytics and Attribution to see who buys and where traffic comes from
cards.summary: Brand Registry unlocks search-term, demographic and cross-purchase reports plus Amazon Attribution for off-Amazon campaigns.
cards.use_when: Measurement: diagnosing which queries, audiences and off-Amazon channels produce Amazon sales.
steps: Open Brand Analytics to see what shoppers search for before buying your products, then feed the highest-intent terms back into titles, A+ copy and manual PPC keywords.
Use the demographics view to understand who buys, which informs imagery, tone and audience targeting in ads and creative.

Review the item comparison, alternate purchase and market basket reports to see what customers compare you against and what they buy alongside: use this for bundle ideas, positioning and competitive gaps.

Use Amazon Attribution when running off-Amazon paid traffic (Google ads, Facebook ads, social) to measure how many visitors from each channel reach the listing and actually purchase, rather than guessing at channel value.
Use these reports as the feedback loop for the keyword and creative decisions made elsewhere in the launch plan.
Confirm which reports your brand currently qualifies for, since availability varies by category and account.
caveats: Report availability and definitions can change; verify inside Seller Central.
Attribution measures a channel's contribution to Amazon sales; it does not prove causality on its own.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Apply Cialdini's six principles of influence to Amazon launch assets
cards.summary: Reciprocity, scarcity, authority, consistency, liking and consensus can each be mapped to a concrete pre-launch and listing tactic.
cards.use_when: Acquisition/offer design: assembling launch messaging, promotions and PDP elements for a new Amazon product.
steps: Reciprocity: give something small first, such as free product to influencers or a free podcast interview slot, so they feel inclined to promote you in return.
Scarcity: cap a launch incentive, for example only 200 units at a discounted price, and tell the email list and social followers the price returns to normal when they sell out.
Authority: use recognized creators or experts to recommend the product, since shoppers follow authority figures' recommendations.
Consistency: get people to join the Facebook group and participate before launch; earlier engagement commitments make them more likely to buy.
Liking: introduce yourself and your brand to the audience through social content, an about-us video, and about-us content on the Amazon page.
Consensus/social proof: get influencers talking about the product, surface group and list members saying positive things, and share real customer stories.
The presenter's 80/20 for a launch: some social or influencer presence, an engaged email list, and a scarcity element on the offer.
caveats: The presenter advises using these principles from a healthy, honest place because they can be used manipulatively.
Scarcity claims must be genuine to avoid misleading customers and platform issues.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx
